domain_label: Turlock & Central Valley Wage-Job Income Ladder
purpose: decide which wage job to pursue in Turlock and Stanislaus County given a person's current skills, documents and constraints, benchmark realistic pay, land the job through the channels employers actually use, and plan the next higher-paying rung
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors grounded in how the Modesto-Turlock (Stanislaus County) labor market is structured
the worker may have limited formal experience, may need flexible or shift hours, and wants the fastest realistic path to higher take-home pay
wage figures are reasoned bands by sector and role, not quoted offers; the worker confirms current numbers with EDD/CalJOBS and the employer
exclusions: commercial driving credentials and driving-instructor licensing (delegated to the paid-driving-credentials KB)
starting one's own business, contracts and equipment (delegated to the service-contract business KB)
immigration or legal advice on work authorization beyond pointing at the documents an employer will require
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for navigating the Turlock/Stanislaus County wage-labor market, reasoned from the region's dominant industries (food processing, agriculture, warehousing/logistics, healthcare, retail, education and public sector) and standard California hiring practice
source_citation: method modeled on EDD Labor Market Information and BLS OEWS occupational wage bands for the Modesto MSA, CalJOBS posting channels, and standard temp-to-hire staffing practice; no proprietary dataset supplied

competency_questions.question: What current skills, documents, hours and transport constraints does this worker have, and what do they gate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SELF_INVENTORY lists skills/constraints and WORK_AUTH_AND_DOCS lists the right-to-work documents an employer will require

competency_questions.question: Which sectors and named employers dominate hiring in Turlock and Stanislaus County?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOCAL_LABOR_SCAN names the dominant sectors and EMPLOYER_TARGETING names concrete large employers and how each hires

competency_questions.question: What is a realistic pay band for a given role locally, including shift and overtime premiums?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WAGE_BENCHMARK gives a reasoned band by role and SHIFT_PREMIUMS adds the night/weekend/overtime uplift

competency_questions.question: What is the fastest low-barrier way to start earning now?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENTRY_SECTORS names low-barrier entry roles and STAFFING_AGENCY_PATH explains temp-to-hire as the fast door

competency_questions.question: Which higher-wage roles are reachable with only short training?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HIGHER_WAGE_TARGETS lists roles reachable in weeks-to-months and CREDENTIAL_ROI shows their pay lift

competency_questions.question: Is a particular certificate or course worth its cost and time?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CREDENTIAL_ROI computes payback from cost, time and wage lift; SKILL_STACKING shows certs to stack while employed

competency_questions.question: Where are the jobs actually posted and how does a person apply effectively?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: APPLICATION_CHANNELS lists the real channels and RESUME_MINIMAL gives the minimal effective application

competency_questions.question: What screening should the worker expect before being hired?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INTERVIEW_BASICS covers drug test/background/physical and WORK_AUTH_AND_DOCS covers the documents to bring

competency_questions.question: How does the worker climb to a better-paid rung once inside?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ON_JOB_LADDER names internal promotion paths and UNION_AND_PUBLIC names union/public routes with benefits

competency_questions.question: How should total compensation and W-2 versus gig pay be compared?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENEFITS_TOTALCOMP values health/PTO/retirement and GIG_VS_W2 weighs stability, taxes and benefits

competency_questions.question: How does the worker avoid dead-end, exploitative or scam offers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AVOID_DEADENDS lists the red flags of wage theft, fake-high-pay and MLM traps

competency_questions.question: What is the worker's 6-12 month income plan and when is it revisited?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INCOME_PLAN sequences entry-now then credential-then-climb with milestones and REASSESS_LOOP sets the review triggers

glossary.definition: the Modesto Metropolitan Statistical Area, covering Stanislaus County including Turlock, the unit used for local wage statistics
a staffing-agency arrangement where a worker starts as a temporary placement and the host employer can convert them to a direct hire after a probation period
California's state job board run by EDD where many local employers and staffing agencies post openings and where unemployment claimants must register
extra hourly pay for working evening, night (graveyard) or weekend shifts, common in food processing and warehousing
the full value of a job including base wage plus health insurance, paid time off, retirement match and other benefits, not just the hourly rate
the return on a training credential, measured as the annual wage lift it unlocks divided by its out-of-pocket cost and the weeks of lost or reduced earning to obtain it
the federal Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics program that publishes wage bands by occupation and metro area, the benchmark source for local pay
the harvest and pack months (roughly summer through fall in the Valley) when food processors and ag employers hire heavily and pay overtime
the identity and employment-authorization documents (such as those on the federal I-9 list) an employer must collect before a worker can start

nodes.definition: Inventory the worker's current marketable skills, certificates, physical capacity, available hours, transport, English level and any scheduling or legal constraints, because every downstream targeting and application choice is gated by what the worker can actually do and when.

pros.claim: An honest inventory prevents chasing roles the worker cannot start and reveals quick wins they already qualify for
pros.example: a worker with a forklift card and own car can target warehouse jobs today instead of waiting on a course

cons.claim: Over-discounting transferable skills can make a capable worker aim too low
cons.example: treating years of unpaid family-business bookkeeping as 'no experience'

failure_modes: transport or childcare constraint discovered only after accepting a graveyard shift
language barrier ignored so applications target English-only roles
acceptance_tests: the inventory lists skills, certificates, available days/hours, transport, and any hard constraints in one place
revisit_triggers: the worker gains a certificate or loses access to transport
available hours change due to childcare or a second job

base.update_signal: the worker's skills, hours, transport or constraints change

nodes.definition: Map the sectors that actually drive hiring in Turlock and Stanislaus County so targeting follows where the jobs are: food and dairy processing, agriculture, warehousing and distribution, healthcare, retail and grocery, education, and city/county public service.

included: which sectors hire continuously vs seasonally

pros.claim: Knowing the local sector mix concentrates effort where openings are dense instead of on thin national listings
pros.example: recognizing food processing and warehousing as the steady volume hirers in the area

cons.claim: A static sector map misses a fast-growing or shrinking employer
cons.example: missing a new distribution center hiring hundreds

failure_modes: chasing a glamorous sector that barely hires locally
ignoring seasonality so applying to ag in the off-season
acceptance_tests: the scan names the top hiring sectors and flags which are continuous versus seasonal
revisit_triggers: a major employer opens or closes locally
a seasonal peak begins or ends

base.update_signal: the local employer or sector mix shifts

nodes.definition: Establish realistic local pay bands by role using OEWS Modesto-MSA occupational wages and California minimum-wage floors as the method, so the worker can tell a fair offer from a lowball and set a target wage that is actually attainable in this market.

included: pay band by role and sector

pros.claim: A reasoned wage band turns 'is this good pay?' into a concrete comparison and anchors negotiation
pros.example: knowing warehouse roles cluster well above minimum lets a worker reject an at-minimum offer

cons.claim: Published bands lag the market and miss signing or retention bumps
cons.example: a tight-labor month where employers pay above the published band

failure_modes: accepting an offer far below the local band for the role
anchoring on a national wage that does not hold in the Valley
acceptance_tests: each target role has a low-mid-high local pay band with the source named
revisit_triggers: California minimum wage changes
OEWS or EDD publishes updated local wages

base.update_signal: local wage data or the minimum-wage floor is updated

nodes.definition: Identify the lowest-barrier roles a worker can start within days to a couple of weeks for immediate income: food-processing line and sanitation, warehouse pick/pack and forklift, retail and grocery stocking, fast food, and entry caregiving, ranked by how fast they convert an application into a paycheck.

included: roles hiring with little or no experience

pros.claim: Securing fast entry income stabilizes the household while a higher-wage plan is built in parallel
pros.example: starting a warehouse temp role this week to fund a CDL course next month

cons.claim: Entry roles can become a comfortable trap that delays the move to higher pay
cons.example: staying years on a starting line wage with no skill-stacking

failure_modes: treating an entry role as the destination not the bridge
picking the lowest-paying entry role when a similar one pays more
acceptance_tests: at least three low-barrier roles the worker qualifies for are listed with speed-to-hire
revisit_triggers: the worker earns a credential that opens a higher entry tier
a seasonal peak opens faster-paying entry work

base.update_signal: the worker's qualifications or the seasonal entry market changes

nodes.definition: Identify higher-wage roles reachable with only weeks-to-months of training that fit the local market: commercial driver, medical assistant or CNA, welder, machine operator, dispatch/logistics coordinator, maintenance tech and HVAC/electrical apprentice, each paired with its training door.

pros.claim: A short-credential target gives the worker a concrete, fundable jump in pay rather than a vague 'get a better job'
pros.example: targeting CNA or forklift-plus-lead to move off minimum within a season

cons.claim: A target role may have a local glut or require a license the worker cannot yet obtain
cons.example: training for a role that locally has few openings

failure_modes: choosing a target with high pay but no local demand
ignoring a licensing barrier discovered only after paying for training
acceptance_tests: each target role names its pay band, training door, and local demand level
revisit_triggers: a target role's local demand or licensing rule changes
the worker completes a credential and needs the next target

base.update_signal: local demand or licensing for a target role changes

nodes.definition: Compute whether a credential pays for itself: payback months equal out-of-pocket cost plus reduced earnings during training, divided by the monthly wage lift it unlocks, so the worker funds the credentials with the shortest payback first and skips ones that never recoup.

excluded: how to study for the credential

pros.claim: Ranking by payback stops money going to expensive credentials with little wage lift
pros.example: choosing a low-cost forklift card with fast payback over a costly course with marginal lift

cons.claim: Payback math undervalues a credential that opens a whole career ladder, not just one raise
cons.example: scoring an apprenticeship only on its first-year bump

failure_modes: paying for a credential whose wage lift never recoups the cost
ignoring free or employer-funded training that beats paying out of pocket
acceptance_tests: each candidate credential has a payback-in-months figure and a fund/skip decision
revisit_triggers: course price or the unlocked wage changes
a free or subsidized training option appears

base.update_signal: training cost or the unlocked wage changes

nodes.definition: Account for the pay levers beyond base rate: evening, night and weekend shift premiums, overtime and double-time rules, and seasonal-peak overtime in food processing and ag, since these can raise take-home well above the headline wage for workers who can take the hours.

pros.claim: Choosing premium shifts can lift take-home by a large margin without any new credential
pros.example: taking a graveyard line shift during pack season for night premium plus overtime

cons.claim: Premium shifts carry health, safety and childcare costs that can outweigh the extra pay
cons.example: chronic sleep loss and unsafe fatigue from sustained graveyard work

failure_modes: banking on seasonal overtime that ends abruptly
ignoring the health/family cost of permanent night shifts
acceptance_tests: the take-home estimate separates base pay from shift and overtime premium
revisit_triggers: the seasonal peak ends
the worker's capacity for night or weekend hours changes

base.update_signal: shift differentials, overtime rules or season change

nodes.definition: Translate the sector map into a concrete shortlist of large local employers and how each actually hires: food and dairy processors, regional distribution centers, hospitals and clinics, the school district, the city and county, and major retailers, with the door (online portal, on-site, agency) for each.

pros.claim: A named-employer shortlist replaces scattered applications with a focused campaign on places that hire in volume
pros.example: applying directly to the three largest local processors and the distribution center portal

cons.claim: Big employers can have slow, automated hiring that filters out strong walk-in candidates
cons.example: an application-tracking system rejecting a capable applicant on keyword match

failure_modes: applying only online when an employer hires through an agency or on-site
ignoring smaller employers that hire faster
acceptance_tests: the shortlist names employers with the correct hiring door for each
revisit_triggers: an employer changes its hiring process
a new large employer enters the area

base.update_signal: an employer's hiring channel or presence changes

nodes.definition: Use the channels through which local jobs are actually filled, in priority order: personal referrals, staffing agencies, on-site and walk-in hiring, CalJOBS and the county job center, employer portals, and the major job boards, because referrals and agencies fill far more local roles than cold online applications.

pros.claim: Leading with referrals and agencies dramatically raises the hit rate versus cold online forms
pros.example: a current employee's referral moving an application to the top of the pile

cons.claim: Relying only on a network can miss openings that are posted but not referred
cons.example: missing a public-sector posting that only appears on the county portal

failure_modes: spraying online applications and waiting instead of working referrals
skipping the free county job center's leads
acceptance_tests: the worker is pursuing at least two high-yield channels, not online forms alone
revisit_triggers: a channel stops producing interviews
the worker builds a new referral contact

base.update_signal: a hiring channel's yield changes

nodes.definition: Use staffing and temp agencies as the fastest door into local warehouse, processing and clerical work, understanding the temp-to-hire model, the agency's cut, the conversion-to-direct-hire path, and the safeguards against agencies that churn workers without ever converting them.

pros.claim: Agencies can place a worker within days and create a direct-hire path that pure applications would take weeks to reach
pros.example: a temp warehouse placement converting to a benefited direct hire after a probation period

cons.claim: Some agencies pay less, offer no benefits and rarely convert, leaving workers stuck as perpetual temps
cons.example: an agency that rotates workers out just before the conversion date

failure_modes: signing with an agency that never converts temps to direct hires
accepting an agency rate well below the direct-hire wage for the same role
acceptance_tests: the chosen agency's conversion terms and pay are confirmed before starting
revisit_triggers: the conversion date passes without an offer
a direct-hire opening for the same role appears

base.update_signal: agency terms or conversion behavior change

nodes.definition: Assemble the identity and employment-authorization documents an employer must collect before a start date (the federal I-9 list), plus a state ID or driver license and any role-specific clearance, so a job offer is not lost to a missing document.

pros.claim: Having documents ready lets a worker accept and start immediately when an offer lands
pros.example: bringing ID and authorization to a same-day orientation

cons.claim: Document gaps can stall a confirmed offer or surface a clearance the worker did not anticipate
cons.example: a food-handling or background clearance delaying a start

failure_modes: losing a start date to a missing or expired document
discovering a role-specific clearance requirement too late
acceptance_tests: the worker has the I-9 documents and any role clearance ready before applying
revisit_triggers: a document expires
a target role adds a clearance requirement

base.update_signal: document validity or a role's clearance rule changes

nodes.definition: Produce the minimal effective application for hourly roles: a one-page resume or a fully completed application form, two or three contactable references, and a no-experience framing that turns school, family-business or volunteer work into relevant reliability signals.

pros.claim: A clean, complete application and ready references clear the basic filters that reject most hourly applicants
pros.example: listing two reachable references and a steady work or school history

cons.claim: Over-investing in resume polish wastes time for roles decided on availability and a passed screening
cons.example: designing a graphic resume for a line job that hires on a one-page form

failure_modes: application rejected as incomplete
references listed who cannot be reached or were not asked
acceptance_tests: the application is complete with reachable references confirmed
revisit_triggers: a reference becomes unreachable
the worker gains new relevant experience to add

base.update_signal: the worker's experience or references change

nodes.definition: Prepare for the screening steps common to local hourly hiring: a short interview focused on reliability and availability, a possible drug test and background check, a physical or lift test for warehouse and processing roles, and basic equipment tests such as a forklift check.

pros.claim: Knowing the screening lets the worker pass it deliberately rather than be surprised out of an offer
pros.example: expecting a lift test and a background check and arriving prepared

cons.claim: Over-coaching can read as inauthentic for roles that simply want a reliable, available worker
cons.example: rehearsed answers where plain reliability was the only ask

failure_modes: a surprise drug test or physical ends a strong candidacy
emphasizing skills when the role screens on availability and reliability
acceptance_tests: the worker knows the screening steps for the target role and can meet each
revisit_triggers: an employer changes its screening
a background or test result needs addressing

base.update_signal: an employer's screening process changes

nodes.definition: Map the internal promotion ladder once hired, because the fastest raises often come from climbing in place: line worker to lead to shift supervisor, picker to inventory or forklift to warehouse lead, with the visible behaviors and certificates that get a worker picked for the next rung.

pros.claim: Internal promotion converts proven reliability into pay without a new job search
pros.example: a dependable line worker promoted to lead within a year

cons.claim: Some employers cap internal mobility, so loyalty yields little and a move pays more
cons.example: a flat structure where leads earn barely above line workers

failure_modes: waiting for a promotion an employer never gives
missing the certificate that gates the next rung
acceptance_tests: the next internal rung and what it requires are identified
revisit_triggers: a promotion is denied or delayed past a set point
a lead or supervisor opening posts internally

base.update_signal: internal promotion openings or criteria change

nodes.definition: Stack low-cost, high-leverage certificates while already earning to compound wage gains: forklift, food-safety handler, OSHA-10, first aid/CPR, and basic spreadsheet or bilingual skills, prioritizing those an employer will pay for or that gate the next promotion.

pros.claim: Cheap certificates earned while employed compound into promotions and side-step the cost of full courses
pros.example: adding a forklift card and OSHA-10 to qualify for a lead role

cons.claim: Collecting certificates with no demand wastes time and money
cons.example: earning a certificate no local employer rewards

failure_modes: paying for a certificate an employer would have funded
stacking certificates that no target role rewards
acceptance_tests: each certificate pursued maps to a promotion or a rewarded skill
revisit_triggers: an employer offers to fund a certificate
a target role changes its required certificates

base.update_signal: certificate demand or employer funding changes

nodes.definition: Evaluate union and public-sector routes that offer above-market benefits and pensions: city and county jobs, the school district, registered apprenticeships in the trades, and unionized warehouse or grocery roles, which trade slower hiring for stability, raises on a schedule and strong benefits.

pros.claim: Public and union roles lock in benefits, scheduled raises and a pension that private hourly work rarely matches
pros.example: a county or district job with health coverage and a defined-benefit pension

cons.claim: Their hiring is slow, competitive and process-heavy, a poor fit when income is needed this week
cons.example: a civil-service process taking months from posting to start

failure_modes: banking only on a slow public hire while bills come due
missing an apprenticeship application window
acceptance_tests: at least one public, union or apprenticeship route is identified with its timeline
revisit_triggers: an apprenticeship or civil-service window opens
a public employer posts a target role

base.update_signal: a public or apprenticeship hiring window changes

nodes.definition: Value the whole offer, not just the wage: convert health insurance, paid time off, retirement match, predictable scheduling and tuition help into a dollar figure so a lower-wage job with strong benefits can be compared honestly against a higher-wage job without them.

pros.claim: Pricing benefits prevents being lured by a higher hourly rate that nets less after buying one's own insurance
pros.example: a benefited job at slightly lower wage beating a bare higher-wage offer after health costs

cons.claim: Benefit values are uncertain and matter less for a worker who needs maximum cash now
cons.example: a pension worth little to someone who will not stay long enough to vest

failure_modes: comparing two offers on wage alone and ignoring benefits
overvaluing a benefit the worker will never use or vest in
acceptance_tests: competing offers are compared on a total-compensation dollar figure, not wage alone
revisit_triggers: an employer changes its benefits
the worker's health or family situation changes the value of benefits

base.update_signal: an offer's benefit package changes

nodes.definition: Weigh 1099 gig and app work (rideshare, delivery, day labor) against a W-2 job on the dimensions that decide real income: self-employment tax and expenses, lack of benefits and unemployment, schedule freedom, and income volatility, so gig work is used as a flexible supplement rather than mistaken for a higher-paying job.

pros.claim: Gig work fills income gaps with instant, flexible hours around a primary job or training
pros.example: delivery shifts on evenings while holding a daytime W-2 role

cons.claim: After self-employment tax, fuel, wear and no benefits, gross gig pay often nets below a steady W-2 wage
cons.example: headline per-hour gig pay shrinking sharply after vehicle costs and taxes

failure_modes: treating gross gig pay as net and quitting a benefited W-2 job
ignoring vehicle depreciation and self-employment tax in the comparison
acceptance_tests: gig pay is compared to W-2 on a net, after-cost, after-tax basis
revisit_triggers: gig pay rates or platform rules change
vehicle or fuel costs change the net materially

base.update_signal: gig economics or platform terms change

nodes.definition: Filter out dead-end and exploitative offers: wage theft and unpaid-training schemes, 'unlimited income' commission-only and MLM pitches, fake high-pay ads that bait-and-switch, and roles with no advancement, so effort is not burned on offers that cannot actually pay.

pros.claim: A red-flag filter protects time and money from offers engineered to extract, not employ
pros.example: rejecting a 'job' that requires buying inventory upfront

cons.claim: An over-strict filter can reject a legitimate commission or probationary role
cons.example: dismissing a real sales role with a base plus commission as a scam

failure_modes: paying upfront for a job that never pays back
staying in a wage-theft situation instead of reporting it
acceptance_tests: any offer requiring upfront payment or promising 'unlimited' income is flagged for scrutiny
revisit_triggers: an offer shows a red flag
a current employer underpays or withholds wages

base.update_signal: a new scam pattern or exploitative offer appears

nodes.definition: Synthesize the analysis into a sequenced 6-to-12 month income plan: secure fast entry income now, run the highest-ROI credential in parallel, then climb via promotion or a targeted move, each step with a date, a pay target and a fallback, so the worker has one concrete ladder rather than scattered options.

included: sequenced milestones with dates and pay targets
excluded: the underlying benchmarks and ROI inputs

pros.claim: A dated, sequenced plan turns analysis into action and makes progress measurable
pros.example: entry job by week two, credential by month three, higher-wage role by month six

cons.claim: An over-rigid plan can blind the worker to a better opportunity that appears off-plan
cons.example: passing up an unexpected apprenticeship to stick to the written sequence

failure_modes: a plan with no dates that never gets executed
no fallback when a step slips
acceptance_tests: the plan has at least three dated milestones each with a pay target and a fallback
revisit_triggers: a milestone is hit or missed
a better off-plan opportunity appears

base.update_signal: a milestone is reached, missed, or a new option appears

nodes.definition: Re-run the relevant parts of the plan on a schedule and on triggers: monthly progress checks, season changes, a completed credential, a denied promotion, or a market shift, so the income ladder stays matched to the worker's situation rather than going stale.

pros.claim: Scheduled reassessment catches stale targets and opens the next rung at the right moment
pros.example: revisiting targets when a credential finishes or a season turns

cons.claim: Reassessing too often churns the plan and undermines steady execution
cons.example: rewriting the plan weekly so nothing is ever completed

failure_modes: never revisiting so the plan goes stale
rewriting the plan so often nothing finishes
acceptance_tests: a review cadence and a trigger list are set and followed
revisit_triggers: a scheduled review date arrives
a material change in skills, market or season occurs

base.update_signal: a review date or material change triggers reassessment

conflict_axes.name: earn_now_vs_train_for_later
conflict_axes.description: immediate income competes with time invested in a credential that pays more later
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stabilize cash with entry work, then protect parallel training time

conflict_axes.name: wage_vs_total_comp
conflict_axes.description: a higher hourly rate can net less than a lower rate with strong benefits
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: compare offers on a total-comp dollar figure, weighted by what the worker will actually use

conflict_axes.name: speed_vs_stability
conflict_axes.description: the fastest job to get is often the least stable or benefited
poles: wait for a stable benefited role
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: bridge with fast work while pursuing the stable role in parallel

conflict_axes.name: premium_shift_vs_health
conflict_axes.description: premium night and weekend hours raise pay but cost sleep, safety and family time
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use premium shifts as a temporary boost, not a permanent baseline

conflict_axes.name: loyalty_vs_jumping
conflict_axes.description: internal promotion rewards loyalty but a market move can pay more faster
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: climb in place where the ladder is real; jump when it is capped

conflict_axes.name: gig_flexibility_vs_net_pay
conflict_axes.description: gig work offers flexible hours but often nets less after costs and taxes
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use gig as a supplement, not a replacement for a benefited W-2 job

conflict_axes.name: agency_speed_vs_conversion_risk
conflict_axes.description: agencies place fast but may never convert temps to direct hires
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: accept agency speed only with confirmed conversion terms

conflict_axes.name: broad_vs_focused_search
conflict_axes.description: wide application volume competes with focused effort on high-yield channels
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: concentrate on the two highest-yield channels before widening

conflict_axes.name: plan_rigidity_vs_opportunism
conflict_axes.description: a fixed plan aids execution but can blind the worker to a better off-plan opening
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the plan but allow a documented override for a clearly better option

edge_cases.description: worker has no transport during graveyard hours
edge_cases.trigger: a premium night role is offered but no ride exists at that hour
edge_cases.mitigation: match shift to available transport or arrange a carpool before accepting

edge_cases.description: credential has no local demand despite high advertised pay
edge_cases.trigger: a target role pays well nationally but has almost no local openings
edge_cases.mitigation: verify local demand before paying for the credential

edge_cases.description: agency churns the worker just before conversion
edge_cases.trigger: the temp assignment ends right before the direct-hire date
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm conversion terms in writing and track the date

edge_cases.description: offer requires upfront payment for training or materials
edge_cases.trigger: a 'job' asks the worker to pay before earning
edge_cases.mitigation: treat upfront payment as a scam signal and decline

edge_cases.description: missing document on the start date
edge_cases.trigger: orientation requires an I-9 document the worker does not have
edge_cases.mitigation: assemble and verify all documents before the start date

edge_cases.description: seasonal overtime ends and income drops sharply
edge_cases.mitigation: plan for the off-season income dip and line up steady work

edge_cases.description: higher wage offer has worse net after losing benefits
edge_cases.trigger: a raise comes with loss of employer health coverage
edge_cases.mitigation: compare on total comp net of self-purchased insurance

edge_cases.trigger: leads earn barely more than line workers
edge_cases.mitigation: switch to a market move once the internal ceiling is clear

edge_cases.description: background check surfaces an old record
edge_cases.trigger: a screening flags a prior issue
edge_cases.mitigation: target fair-chance employers and prepare an honest explanation

edge_cases.description: public-sector hire is too slow for urgent bills
edge_cases.trigger: a civil-service process runs months while rent is due
edge_cases.mitigation: bridge with entry income while the slow hire proceeds

edge_cases.description: language barrier filters out otherwise-qualified worker
edge_cases.mitigation: target bilingual-friendly employers and add an ESL track to the plan

workflow.action: inventory skills, documents, hours and constraints
workflow.description: capture what the worker can do and when before targeting
workflow.gate: skills, hours, transport and constraints are all recorded

workflow.action: map local sectors and named employers
workflow.description: identify where local hiring is concentrated
workflow.gate: dominant sectors and at least five named employers listed

workflow.description: set low-mid-high bands for each candidate role
workflow.gate: every candidate role has a sourced pay band

workflow.description: land a low-barrier role to stabilize cash now
workflow.artifact: active application or accepted entry role
workflow.gate: at least one entry role is applied to or started

workflow.action: select a higher-wage target and price its credential
workflow.description: choose the best short-credential jump by payback
workflow.gate: a target role and a funded credential with payback are chosen

workflow.description: lead with referrals and agencies over cold forms
workflow.gate: at least two high-yield channels are active

workflow.description: ready the resume, references, documents and screening
workflow.gate: application is complete and screening steps are anticipated

workflow.description: value benefits in dollars before deciding
workflow.gate: competing offers compared on total comp, not wage alone

workflow.action: filter out dead-end and scam offers
workflow.description: apply the red-flag filter to every offer
workflow.gate: no offer with upfront-payment or unlimited-income flags advances

workflow.description: sequence entry, credential and climb with dates
workflow.gate: at least three dated milestones with pay targets and fallbacks
a review schedule and trigger list are in place

dominance_rules.rule: when cash is urgent, fast entry income outranks waiting for a better role
dominance_rules.rationale: an unstable household cannot execute any longer-term plan
dominance_rules.trigger: rent or essentials are at risk this month
dominance_rules.action: take the fastest legitimate entry role while pursuing the better one in parallel

dominance_rules.rule: total compensation outranks headline wage in any offer comparison
dominance_rules.rationale: benefits and stability change real take-home more than the hourly number
dominance_rules.action: decide on the total-comp dollar figure, not the wage alone

dominance_rules.rule: a credential with no local demand is rejected regardless of its advertised pay
dominance_rules.rationale: pay that does not exist locally cannot be earned
dominance_rules.trigger: a target role lacks local openings
dominance_rules.action: drop the credential and pick a locally demanded target

dominance_rules.rule: any offer requiring upfront payment is treated as a scam until proven otherwise
dominance_rules.rationale: legitimate jobs pay the worker, not the reverse
dominance_rules.trigger: an offer asks for money upfront
dominance_rules.action: decline or demand proof before any payment

dominance_rules.rule: confirmed conversion terms are required before accepting an agency placement as a path to direct hire
dominance_rules.rationale: temp-only churn wastes months without a permanent role
dominance_rules.action: get conversion terms in writing or treat it as temp-only

dominance_rules.rule: referrals and agencies are worked before cold online applications
dominance_rules.rationale: these channels fill most local roles and have far higher hit rates
dominance_rules.action: activate referral and agency channels first

dominance_rules.rule: documents and screening readiness must precede applying for a role with a hard start date
dominance_rules.rationale: a missing document forfeits a won offer
dominance_rules.trigger: applying to a role that hires fast
dominance_rules.action: ready I-9 documents and anticipate screening before applying

dominance_rules.rule: climb in place only while the internal ladder is real; otherwise move
dominance_rules.rationale: loyalty to a capped ladder forgoes attainable pay
dominance_rules.trigger: the next internal rung pays little more
dominance_rules.action: switch to a targeted market move

dominance_rules.rule: premium night shifts are temporary boosts, not a permanent default
dominance_rules.rationale: sustained graveyard work harms health and promotion visibility
dominance_rules.trigger: premium shifts become the standing schedule
dominance_rules.action: rotate toward day shifts when a promotion is reachable

anti_rework_rules.rule: inventory skills and documents before targeting roles
anti_rework_rules.prevents: chasing roles the worker cannot start or losing an offer to a missing document

anti_rework_rules.rule: verify local demand before paying for any credential
anti_rework_rules.prevents: spending on training that unlocks no local job

anti_rework_rules.rule: benchmark the local wage band before accepting an offer
anti_rework_rules.prevents: taking a lowball offer below the going local rate

anti_rework_rules.rule: confirm agency conversion terms before starting a temp placement
anti_rework_rules.prevents: months lost as a non-converting perpetual temp

anti_rework_rules.rule: compare offers on total comp before deciding
anti_rework_rules.prevents: switching for a higher wage that nets less after lost benefits

anti_rework_rules.rule: apply the scam filter before engaging any offer
anti_rework_rules.prevents: time and money lost to upfront-payment and MLM traps

anti_rework_rules.rule: secure entry income before committing full time to slow public hiring
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a cash gap while a months-long civil-service process runs

anti_rework_rules.rule: ready documents and anticipate screening before a hard-start application
anti_rework_rules.prevents: forfeiting a won offer on the start date

iteration_protocol.action: re-run target selection and the income plan to the next rung

iteration_protocol.trigger: a seasonal peak begins or ends
iteration_protocol.action: adjust entry and shift-premium choices for the season

iteration_protocol.trigger: an internal promotion is denied or delayed
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate climbing in place versus a market move

iteration_protocol.trigger: minimum wage or local wage data updates
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the wage benchmark and re-rank options

iteration_protocol.trigger: an offer shows a scam red flag
iteration_protocol.action: filter the offer and prune the employer shortlist

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-yield channel stops producing interviews
iteration_protocol.action: shift effort to other channels and build new referrals

iteration_protocol.trigger: a scheduled monthly review date arrives
iteration_protocol.action: check milestone progress and update the plan

priority_rationale: foundational inventory, sector and wage work precede targeting and landing, which precede advancement, decision and the synthesized plan, so the worker stabilizes income before building the higher-wage ladder.
